subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support a default-off Slack user-account DM mode that receives and replies as a regular Slack user identity?
rationale: This changes Slack identity, authorization, and audit boundaries; code inspection shows the current product intentionally keeps bot-token routing as the default and user-token writes as a fallback.

options.title: Add explicit user-account DM mode
options.body: Implement a Slack-plugin mode with clear config, authorization mapping, xoxp reply selection, docs, tests, and security guardrails while preserving bot/app defaults.

options.title: Keep bot/app identity only
options.body: Document that user tokens remain read/fallback credentials and close or defer user-identity DM control as outside the current security posture.

options.title: Prototype behind maintainer-only review
options.body: Allow an experimental branch or design issue first, but do not queue an autonomous fix until the identity and scope policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Add explicit user-account DM mode
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack-plugin mode with clear config, authorization mapping, xoxp reply selection, docs, tests, and security guardrails while preserving bot/app defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original user-token behavior and has adjacent Slack/channel-boundary history, making him the best available routing owner for the product/security decision.
